correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts every \(\Omega\le2\) factorization shape. The even member is \(2\), \(4\), or \(2p\). For \(2p\), \(\lambda(2p)=p-1\); the adjacent odd member is prime, a prime square, or \(qr\). The first two are excluded directly. For \(qr\), writing \(d=\gcd(q-1,r-1)\) gives \(\lambda(qr)=(q-1)(r-1)/d\), and both adjacency signs yield a contradiction because \(d\ge2\) and \(d\le q-1\).

value.rationale: Consecutive repeated values are a standard local problem for arithmetic functions, and Carmichael's function has an explicit run-length literature. The theorem identifies the exact first multiplicative-complexity layer: after \((3,4)\), every coincidence forces at least one argument to have \(\Omega\ge3\). This is a natural structural threshold and an unrestricted classification within that layer.
